events.$comment: Arrays because a rig that accepts one spelling and dies on a synonym is a rig that fails the day somebody is right.

$comment: The core answers an unrecognised stdin line on stderr by name. The rig
sends a word that cannot ever be real and looks for this sentence, then
sends each M3 word and asserts the sentence does NOT appear: that is how a
word that was never wired is told apart from one that was.
stderr.unknownWord: is not a command this build understands on stdin

exitCodes.$comment: 130 is the second-stop exit, the one that abandons the batch in flight. After a detach it is a bug.

$runValueName: The Run VALUE NAME is productName, and productName is the human display
name from M3 onwards: Photo Pigeon, with the space. The machine
identifiers did not move: the exe is still photo-pigeon.exe and the
install directory is still what the bundler makes of the product name.
The rig does not depend on this: it finds photo-pigeon entries by the exe
their DATA names, which survives a rename of the product.
$bootFlag: Settled at M3 in app/src-tauri/src/autostart.rs (BOOT_FLAG), against
section 4's --hidden. There is no window at any launch, so --hidden has
nothing to hide; the flag's only job is to say the launch came from the
$nameEnv: The environment variable that moves the Run VALUE NAME aside so a test can
watch the shell write one without ever touching the real entry. If the
shell does not read it, every tray scenario in run-m3.ps1 refuses to launch
rather than risk writing the production value name on this machine.
$shellLogBootMarker: A substring the shell writes to its own log when it recognises the boot
flag. It is how the rig proves the word that ships is the word the boot
path really parses, which is the disagreement M3 had to settle. Absent, the
check is a warning rather than a pass, because a silent log is not proof.
